rules: Every proven feature has a model or positive witness.
Every accepted boundary has a nearest rejected or malformed witness.
Runtime facts do not imply Android framework or device behavior.
Unknown features never count as a support claim.
Release tier uses selected producer/hardening witnesses, not a blind Cartesian product.
Legacy Wrapper v1 and Android JNI/native-bridge observations remain baseline evidence, not HostContext compatibility claims.

features.obligation: ELF64 little-endian AArch64 ET_DYN identity and bounded load map
The ELF parser classifies bounded AArch64 ET_EXEC images as observation data without implying outer launch or HostContext support.
constraints: This row proves parser/model observation only. Outer acceptance is separately recorded as elf.outer.dynamic-et-exec; static ET_EXEC remains un-packable and HostContext remains ET_DYN-only.

features.obligation: Each AArch64 ET_DYN PT_LOAD with p_align greater than one uses a power-of-two alignment and congruent p_offset and p_vaddr residues, including non-page-sized alignment
outer-execveat accepts only dynamic AArch64 ET_EXEC executables with a supported native interpreter and preserves native process behavior through anonymous execveat handoff
constraints: Accepted predicate: AArch64 ELF64 little-endian ET_EXEC, executable entry in PT_LOAD, PT_DYNAMIC, PT_INTERP with an absolute path ending in ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 or ld-musl-aarch64.so.1, and no RPATH/RUNPATH.
Shared objects, static ET_EXEC, missing PT_INTERP, and unrecognized interpreters remain rejected.
This is outer-wrapper evidence only; HostContext semantics and frame ABI are unchanged.

features.obligation: PT_DYNAMIC and dynamic metadata are mapped and bounded
The managed ELF parser bounds and models DT_VERDEF/DT_VERDEFNUM records and their dynamic-string-table auxiliaries as parser observation only.
constraints: The registry-baseline declaredFeatureCoverage cue is symbol-versions: 7; it is expected-tag coverage, not confirmed ELF prevalence or product support evidence.
The checked-in positive fixture path is tests/UrProtect.Core.Tests/Fixtures/SymbolVersions/liburp-versioned.so with SHA-256 4fb8ffa362ce8a18590eff735c971aaf217eb4dcd338bf071810fe0b3c971ae8.
The checked-in registry-baseline featureHistogram contains only identity and loader facts; actual CI fingerprint histogram evidence remains required for later frequency-based selection or promotion.

This row proves bounded parser/model observation for definitions only. Dependency-side version requirements have a separate runtime.host-context.dependency-symbol-version-requirements row; versioned definitions and entry selection remain rejected.

features.obligation: The managed ELF model bounds and records DT_VERNEED/DT_VERNEEDNUM records, their dynamic-string-table filenames, and version auxiliaries without inferring runtime resolution
constraints: The positive parser oracle asserts the version-need file name and bounded auxiliary name/index; malformed, unmapped, truncated, or inconsistent chains report VersionNeedTableMalformed or SymbolVersionTableMalformed.
This is parser/model evidence only. It does not define loader resolution or HostContext acceptance; runtime acceptance is limited to runtime.host-context.dependency-symbol-version-requirements.

features.obligation: The narrow HostContext adapter accepts AArch64 RELATIVE/RELR relocation targets in writable load segments and delegates application to the native loader
constraints: AArch64 RELA entries must be NONE or RELATIVE with symbol index zero
RELR targets must be aligned and writable
Dynamic flag entries allow only immediate binding flags
The system loader remains responsible for applying accepted relocations

features.obligation: The HostContext adapter accepts the bounded AArch64 GLOB_DAT symbolic relocation form with a checked dynamic symbol table entry and writable relocation target
constraints: The first symbolic slice accepts R_AARCH64_GLOB_DAT with a nonzero symbol index, DT_SYMTAB/DT_SYMENT metadata, a file-backed symbol entry, and an aligned writable relocation target.
The system loader remains responsible for resolving and applying the relocation; the retained oracle proves the real profile-matched entry dispatch returns status 29.

PLT relocations are separately bounded by runtime.host-context.weak-undefined-jump-slot; the single-libc import-version subset is separately bounded by runtime.host-context.dependency-symbol-version-requirements, while other symbol-binding and versioned-entry combinations remain explicit boundaries.

features.obligation: The HostContext adapter accepts only DT_JMPREL/DT_PLTRELSZ/DT_PLTREL=DT_RELA tuples containing R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT for a file-backed undefined weak default-visible STT_FUNC symbol, with no DT_NEEDED or symbol-version tags, and the native loader resolves the function to zero
constraints: This is an exact weak-undefined function JUMP_SLOT slice, not generic PLT/JUMP_SLOT support: table tags are present together, entries are exact-size RELA, targets are aligned writable in-image addresses, and dynsym records are file-backed and exact-size.

The symbol must be STB_WEAK, STT_FUNC, exact STV_DEFAULT st_other, and SHN_UNDEF. The image has no DT_NEEDED entries and no DT_VERSYM/DT_VERDEF/DT_VERDEFNUM/DT_VERNEED/DT_VERNEEDNUM tags; other combinations remain rejected.

Binding is immediate (DF_BIND_NOW or DF_1_NOW); the adapter uses RTLD_NOW. Lookup uses the native loader global scope followed by this image's declared dependencies (none in this subset); an unresolved weak function resolves to zero.
The real AArch64 glibc managed HostContext entry confirms the unresolved weak function is zero and returns status 53. Negative mutations require a zero image handle before loader handoff.

features.obligation: A valid ET_DYN remains parseable when section headers are absent; program headers remain authoritative
A HostContext AArch64 ET_DYN remains loadable when section headers are absent; program headers and dynamic metadata remain authoritative
constraints: The image must still provide bounded AArch64 PT_LOAD and PT_DYNAMIC program headers
This validates the native adapter slice and does not claim broader loader behavior

features.obligation: A bounded PT_GNU_RELRO program header has a file-backed range inside the AArch64 image with p_memsz >= p_filesz, and the retained image completes HostContext entry dispatch
constraints: The self-test covers only a bounded PT_GNU_RELRO program-header file range and p_memsz >= p_filesz
The unmodified image retaining PT_GNU_RELRO must dispatch through the real adapter with status 23
Memory protection semantics remain delegated to the native system loader; this is validated implementation evidence, not proof of a custom RELRO implementation

features.obligation: The HostContext adapter accepts a PT_GNU_STACK program header when PF_X is clear and rejects an executable PT_GNU_STACK before creating an image handle
constraints: The real fixture must contain PT_GNU_STACK with PF_X clear and must complete HostContext dispatch through the unchanged adapter path
The self-test sets only the PT_GNU_STACK p_flags PF_X bit in one bounded image copy and requires URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED with a zero image handle before loading

Memory protection remains delegated to the native system loader for the accepted non-executable GNU_STACK case; this is validated implementation evidence, not proof of custom stack-protection semantics

features.obligation: The release-tier GCC AArch64 PIE witness is built with full GNU RELRO and immediate binding and retains that ELF hardening in the release artifact.
constraints: This is one deliberate release producer/hardening witness, not a compiler/runtime Cartesian product.
The existing gcc-c fixture builder supplies the source and execution path; the release-hardened variant adds -z relro -z now.
The runner readelf oracle requires GNU_RELRO and BIND_NOW before baseline/copy comparison.

features.obligation: AArch64 dynamically linked PIE runs on the recorded native glibc host
AArch64 dynamically linked PIE runs with the recorded musl loader
AArch64 PIE is executed by the pinned bionic linker using a pinned Termux compiler package set whose downloaded artifacts match locked SHA-256 digests.
constraints: The OCI image digest and Termux source revision are pinned.
Clang and every package newly installed to provide its compiler/linker are version- and SHA-256-locked in the manifest and verified before installation.

The Termux package index is used only to locate those locked artifacts; a missing, changed, or additional package fails the lane, while the complete before/after installed package inventories and license identifiers are retained.

features.obligation: Versioned HostContext v1 callbacks and the legacy frame provide immutable AArch64 ET_DYN image loading and explicit entry dispatch for the declared adapter slice; the native adapter enforces image-byte immutability with verified memfd seals before loader handoff.
constraints: The native adapter creates the memfd with MFD_ALLOW_SEALING, adds F_SEAL_WRITE/F_SEAL_SHRINK/F_SEAL_GROW/F_SEAL_SEAL after the complete verified write, verifies F_GET_SEALS, and fails closed before dlopen when any seal operation is unavailable or incomplete.
No PT_INTERP or DT_NEEDED semantics; constructor/destructor tags use the separate runtime.host-context.constructor-destructor rejection boundary
RPATH/RUNPATH tags use the separate runtime.host-context.path-search rejection boundary
Dynamic flags are limited to immediate binding flags; runtime.host-context.unsupported-relocation-table is the dedicated rejection boundary for unsupported relocation-table tags
Only checked AArch64 RELATIVE/RELR relocation targets are accepted; application and memory protection are delegated to the recorded native system loader

features.obligation: HostContext frame v2 carries the ABI, required capabilities, and bounded entry symbol through one frame-relative layout and dispatches the declared entry without a temporary executable path
constraints: The legacy v1 and HostContext v2 layouts remain migration evidence only
Current v3 reserved fields must be zero and unknown profile, ABI, or capability bits are rejected before image loading
Entry and source names are bounded strict UTF-8 values without path components; profile selection is explicit
The current packaging contract uses profile-matched v3 launchers; stale versions and profile/launcher mismatches fail closed.

features.obligation: The production managed pack command selects the current v3 host-context-entry profile and a matching launcher, verifies the sealed in-process handoff, dispatches urp_entry once, releases the image, and preserves its status.
constraints: The current frame is v3 with an explicit host-context-entry profile and bounded urp_entry metadata.
The launcher uses a sealed memfd adapter and the system loader; the retained oracle verifies status 23, clean streams, and the managed report profile/version.
This row proves the declared glibc/native AArch64 adapter slice; bionic remains separately evidenced by runtime.host-context.bionic-handoff.

features.obligation: The pinned native ARM64 Termux userspace builds and runs the HostContext adapter oracle, verifying sealed memfd image loading, real entry dispatch, release, and no executable temporary pathname
constraints: The native adapter test builds the HostContext entry shared object in the pinned Termux userspace and runs the current HostContext frame through /system/bin/linker64's bionic dlopen implementation.
The real adapter must add and verify F_SEAL_WRITE, F_SEAL_SHRINK, F_SEAL_GROW, and F_SEAL_SEAL before dlopen, dispatch urp_entry with its declared status, and release the image handle.
The self-test is an adapter-level HostContext runtime witness; it remains a separate bionic fact from the managed native-glibc production-pack oracle.

features.obligation: Recovered bytes reach the runtime without an executable temporary pathname
An interpreter outside the declared AArch64 host runtimes is refused
features.reason: The current no-path contract does not define dependency resolution for arbitrary interpreters.

features.obligation: The HostContext adapter accepts the bounded AArch64 initial-exec PT_TLS slice and preserves a TLS-backed entry result
constraints: The first slice is AArch64 initial-exec TLS with a structurally bounded PT_TLS segment and R_AARCH64_TLS_TPREL64 relocation; the system loader owns module allocation and initialization.
The retained managed v3 oracle proves the TLS-backed entry returns status 43 on the native glibc lane.
Dynamic TLS models, new-thread initialization, reentrancy, and unload with live TLS users remain outside this slice.

features.obligation: The HostContext adapter accepts the bounded AArch64 GNU property BTI note and dispatches a BTI-instrumented entry image
constraints: The first slice accepts a GNU property note containing only AArch64 FEATURE_1 BTI/PAC bits and rejects unknown feature bits or malformed notes.
The fixture is compiled with AArch64 BTI instrumentation; the retained managed v3 oracle proves entry status 47 on the native glibc lane.
PAC negotiation beyond the note mask and host instruction-state conflicts remain outside this slice.

features.obligation: The HostContext adapter accepts the bounded single-system-libc dependency slice with no payload-controlled path-search metadata and preserves dependency-backed entry dispatch
constraints: The first slice accepts exactly one DT_NEEDED system libc basename (libc.so.6, libc.so, libc.musl-aarch64.so.1, or libc.so.1), with bounded DT_STRTAB/DT_STRSZ metadata and no RPATH/RUNPATH.
Search roots are the native system loader's fixed default roots; payload-controlled path-search metadata remains rejected.
The retained managed v3 oracle proves the real dependency-backed entry returns status 37; other dependency graphs, filters, and auxiliary dependencies remain rejected.

features.obligation: The HostContext adapter accepts only a DT_GNU_HASH-backed, bounded DT_VERSYM/DT_VERNEED/DT_VERNEEDNUM import chain whose version-need files match the existing DT_NEEDED libc.so.6 dependency, and the native system loader resolves it during RTLD_NOW
constraints: This slice requires the exact already-accepted DT_NEEDED basename libc.so.6, no DT_SYMBOLIC, a complete DT_GNU_HASH/DT_VERSYM/DT_VERNEED/DT_VERNEEDNUM tuple, a fully file-backed VERSYM table bounded by the dynamic symbol count, bounded version-need and auxiliary chains, nonempty version names with valid ELF hashes and indices, no weak-version flags, and every vn_file exactly matching libc.so.6.

Versioned images require DT_GNU_HASH; DT_HASH-only and combined SysV hash images are outside this validated slice. GNU-hash symbol counts, DT_VERNEED records, and aggregate Vernaux entries are capped at 1,048,576 by native preflight; over-cap or malformed ranges return LOAD_FAILED.

DT_VERDEF and DT_VERDEFNUM remain rejected; version requirements on recognized non-glibc libc sonames are rejected; HostContext entry selection continues to use the declared unversioned symbol name. The slice does not add dependencies, search paths, or versioned entry lookup.

The native system loader resolves imported libc version requirements during RTLD_NOW. Retained runtime evidence is native AArch64 glibc only; availability of any requested GLIBC version is determined by that host and loader failures remain LOAD_FAILED.
The managed parser separately proves typed VersionNeed records. Native nearest-negative mutations require stable rejection and a zero handle before loader handoff.

features.obligation: On native AArch64 glibc, HostContext accepts exactly the unique direct dependency pair libc.so.6 and ld-linux-aarch64.so.1, dispatches the entry, and releases the sealed root image; unsupported names, duplicates, excess nodes, path tags, and loader influence fail before handoff.
constraints: The accepted graph contains exactly one libc.so.6 and one ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 in either order. It rejects duplicates, third names, unknown names, path tags, DT_AUXILIARY, and DT_FILTER before memfd creation.
The legacy singleton libc slice, including its four historically recognized libc basenames and exact libc.so.6 import-version semantics, remains unchanged.
LD_LIBRARY_PATH, LD_PRELOAD, and LD_AUDIT must be unset or empty for the pair; each nonempty value returns URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED with a zero handle before memfd creation.
The pre-existing single-libc fixture still loads and releases with a nonempty LD_LIBRARY_PATH, confirming the environment predicate is scoped to the new pair only.
The pair is a closed native AArch64 glibc graph only. The system loader shares its process-namespace libc and loader objects; HostContext owns and releases only its sealed entry-image root handle.

No RPATH/RUNPATH, $ORIGIN, arbitrary roots, recursive graph, musl graph, or bionic graph support is inferred. Nonempty LD_LIBRARY_PATH, LD_PRELOAD, or LD_AUDIT is rejected before memfd creation for the new pair.

The native oracle tests both DT_NEEDED orders, observes the root destructor after release, verifies all three environment negatives are rejected before memfd creation by comparing the test-visible attempt count, and forces a post-memfd RTLD_NOW failure to assert LOAD_FAILED, zero handle, and no descriptor leak.

A separate dlopen probe confirms the controlled fake ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 constructor marker works; the managed wrapper is then run with the fake object on LD_LIBRARY_PATH and must return status 4 before handoff with no fake-loader or fixture marker.

The managed oracle records clean empty stdout/stderr in graph-result.txt together with entry status 37 and successful release; empty streams are not standalone evidence artifacts. graph-env-result.txt retains the fake-loader rejection status and no-dispatch result.
The native adapter oracle explicitly looks up and calls entry status 37, invokes release_image and requires URP_STATUS_OK; the managed v3 oracle also returns status 37 after HostContext teardown.

features.obligation: The HostContext adapter delegates the bounded constructor-before-entry and destructor-before-release ordering to the native system loader
constraints: The system loader runs nonzero DT_INIT/DT_INIT_ARRAY metadata before urp_entry and DT_FINI/DT_FINI_ARRAY metadata during release.
The fixture observes constructor state in entry and writes a release marker from the destructor; reentrancy and live-thread teardown remain outside this slice.
Malformed zero-valued lifecycle mutations remain rejected by the native self-test.

features.obligation: The HostContext v1 system-loader adapter rejects DT_RPATH and DT_RUNPATH dynamic path-search metadata before path search or image-handle creation
features.reason: HostContext v1 and the current system-loader adapter define no dynamic path-search roots, ordering, or precedence semantics for in-process images; loader path resolution alone is not a compatibility proof.
constraints: The unchanged non-path-search entry fixture remains the positive HostContext dispatch baseline.

Each bounded dynamic-table mutation changes only one DT_NULL tag, preserves surrounding bytes, initializes a nonzero sentinel handle, and must return URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED with a zero handle before loader handoff.
Constructor/destructor lifecycle metadata and runtime.host-context.unsupported-relocation-table remain separate rejection boundaries.

features.obligation: The HostContext v1 system-loader adapter rejects DT_TEXTREL writable-text relocation metadata before writable-text relocation or image-handle creation
features.reason: HostContext v1 and the current system-loader adapter define no writable-text relocation or W^X/protection semantics for in-process images; loader acceptance alone is not a compatibility proof.
constraints: The unchanged non-text-relocation entry fixture remains the positive HostContext dispatch baseline.

A bounded dynamic-table mutation changes only one DT_NULL tag to DT_TEXTREL, preserves surrounding bytes, initializes a nonzero sentinel handle, and must return URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED with a zero handle before loader handoff.
AArch64 RELATIVE/RELR relocation acceptance and application delegation remain the separate validated elf.relocation.aarch64-relative feature.
Unsupported relocation-table tags use the separate runtime.host-context.unsupported-relocation-table rejection boundary.
No positive text-relocation HostContext fixture or support claim exists until writable-text relocation and W^X/protection semantics are defined by the Host Contract.

features.obligation: The HostContext v1 system-loader adapter rejects DT_REL, DT_RELSZ, and DT_RELENT metadata, and rejects every partial, malformed, or out-of-slice PLT RELA tuple before relocation processing or image-handle creation
features.reason: HostContext v1 defines only checked RELATIVE/RELR plus the separately validated exact weak-undefined JUMP_SLOT subset. Legacy REL and all partial, malformed, versioned, dependency-bearing, or otherwise out-of-slice PLT tables remain rejected.
constraints: The unchanged RELATIVE/RELR entry fixture remains the positive HostContext dispatch baseline.

Each bounded dynamic-table mutation changes only one DT_NULL tag, preserves surrounding bytes, initializes a nonzero sentinel handle, and must return URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED with a zero handle before loader handoff.

The validated elf.relocation.aarch64-relative feature covers checked AArch64 RELATIVE/RELR targets, and runtime.host-context.weak-undefined-jump-slot covers only the exact separately specified PLT subset.
DT_REL/DT_RELSZ/DT_RELENT remain rejected; partial/duplicate/inconsistent PLT tuples, malformed PLT contents, and JUMP_SLOT in ordinary DT_RELA are covered by the PLT negative oracle.

features.obligation: The HostContext v1 adapter rejects DT_ANDROID_REL, DT_ANDROID_RELSZ, DT_ANDROID_RELA, DT_ANDROID_RELASZ, DT_ANDROID_RELR, DT_ANDROID_RELRSZ, DT_ANDROID_RELRENT, and DT_ANDROID_RELRCOUNT before relocation processing or image-handle creation
features.reason: HostContext v1 defines only checked AArch64 RELATIVE/RELR relocation semantics; Android packed relocation encodings have no adapter contract and are rejected before system-loader handoff.
constraints: Each bounded dynamic-table mutation changes only one DT_NULL tag, preserves surrounding bytes, initializes a nonzero sentinel handle, and must return URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED with a zero handle before loader handoff.
The unchanged RELATIVE/RELR entry fixture remains the positive relocation baseline; Android packed relocation forms are not included in elf.relocation.aarch64-relative.
No positive Android packed relocation HostContext fixture or support claim exists until the Host Contract defines these encodings and their application semantics.

features.obligation: The HostContext v1 adapter rejects DT_VERDEF/DT_VERDEFNUM versioned definitions and rejects DT_VERSYM/DT_VERNEED/DT_VERNEEDNUM outside the separately validated libc.so.6 import-requirement slice
features.reason: HostContext v1 does not define versioned entry lookup or versioned exports. Only import-side requirements for the existing libc.so.6 dependency are separately validated; all version definitions and out-of-slice requirement tables remain unsupported.
constraints: The unversioned no-dependency fixture changes one bounded DT_NULL tag per DT_VER* mutation, initializes a nonzero handle sentinel, and requires URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED with a zero handle; the versioned libc.so.6 dependency fixture is tested under its separate exact accepted subset.

DT_VERDEF/DT_VERDEFNUM are rejected even with a libc dependency; DT_VERSYM/DT_VERNEED/DT_VERNEEDNUM are accepted only as the complete, bounded libc.so.6-matched requirement tuple described by runtime.host-context.dependency-symbol-version-requirements.
The declared entry name remains unversioned. No version negotiation for HostContext entry selection or versioned definitions is claimed.

features.obligation: arm64-v8a JNI library loads through the recorded x86_64 Android native bridge
constraints: This is the existing JNI/native-bridge baseline; it does not execute packed output or prove a native ARM64 Android device/runtime.

features.obligation: The existing Wrapper 0.2 managed v1 frame and launcher behavior remain a regression baseline separate from the in-process HostContext v2 contract.
constraints: Legacy v1 retains its wrapper-absolute offset and the managed pack path leaves HostContext metadata null.
This baseline is not an in-process HostContext support claim and does not add a platform compatibility profile.
